intention: analytics.vehicle_monthly_metrics holds one row per vehicle per month: distance, efficiency and battery use split into all days / weekdays / weekends, the month's external-charge and supercharger totals with three ending-battery distributions, and the pack capacity charging measured that month. One idempotent use case takes (tesla_id, period) and rewrites the row, so any port or process can re-sync one month for one car. The nightly job calls it for the current and previous month. Linear MAG-73.
request: /kkpa-pickup-linear-ticket MAG-73 — Analytics monthly metrics table: distance, efficiency and copied capacity. Build the wider monthly metrics table in analytics (backlog item 29, deferred from MAG-32 / RM52 by RD12). One row per vehicle per month storing: total distance from vehicle_metrics.distance_traveled_km_calc plus weekday/weekend splits and per-day averages; efficiency from km_per_pct_calc plus weekday/weekend; battery consumed from consumed_pct plus weekday/weekend; effective capacity COPIED from charging.monthly_effective_capacity.effective_capacity_kwh (a copy, not a read-time join); external-charge energy, cost and session counts split by charger type AC/DC with an ext_ prefix; supercharger energy, cost and session counts with an sc_ prefix; and a JSONB per source holding session counts bucketed by ending battery level (0-20/20-40/40-60/60-80/80-100) for a bar-style view. Runs as a new step 5 in internal/app/processor.go, after step 4, because it reads both step 3's vehicle_metrics and step 4's monthly_effective_capacity. Must be a new, well-named Go type built with the golang skills, isolated and easy to test, taking a single tesla_id and a period (YYYY-MM) as a hexagonal input port, so a period can be re-synced on demand. The ticket asked for /grill-me on five open questions before any artifact: the efficiency formula, the refresh rule when analytics recalculates old months, the month boundary given metric_date, what happens when the capacity is NULL, and the final table name.

decisions.decision: Full ticket scope, four tiers. Tier 2's single migration creates EVERY column, including the ext_*, sc_* and JSONB columns tier 3 fills.
decisions.why: The owner chose the whole ticket over a smaller cut. One migration settles the table shape once; an unfilled column reads as 0, which RD4 makes valid.

decisions.decision: Monthly efficiency is SUM(distance_traveled_km_calc) / SUM(consumed_pct) over days with consumed_pct > 0. Same rule for the weekday and weekend figures. km_per_pct_calc itself is unchanged.
decisions.why: An average of daily ratios weighs a 5 km day like a 300 km day. Owner's worked example: avg of ratios 3.5, real figure 305/55 = 5.5.

decisions.decision: The nightly job syncs TWO periods per vehicle every night: the current month and the previous month. Supersedes the ticket's 'first day of the month only'. The current month's row is knowingly incomplete and carries no completeness flag.
decisions.why: Cost stays flat at 2 x vehicles per night whatever the history length. Owner raised the many-vehicles cost and proposed this window.

decisions.decision: Every column is NOT NULL DEFAULT 0. No nullable columns.
decisions.why: The ticket's literal text, confirmed after the owner saw the cost: it inverts the module's sparse convention, so a 0 efficiency cannot be told from no data by value alone. RD5 recovers that.

decisions.decision: A row is written for every month in the refresh window, including a month with no input, and the table carries at least one count column recording how many vehicle_metrics days fed the row.
decisions.why: RD4 removed NULL as the unknown signal, so a count carries it. charging.monthly_effective_capacity already does this with candidate_count / sample_count.

decisions.decision: The month bucket is metric_date itself: March is metric_date BETWEEN '2026-03-01' AND '2026-03-31'. No day shifting. Weekday/weekend come from the ISO day of week of that DATE; weekend is Saturday and Sunday.
decisions.why: Not a choice. internal/analytics/AGENTS.md forbids re-projecting a returned Date; metric_date already carries the day-before adjustment.

decisions.decision: The table is analytics.vehicle_monthly_metrics, not analytics.monthly_metrics.
decisions.why: It sits beside analytics.vehicle_metrics and the pair reads by itself. It is also the name RM52's RD12 recorded when it deferred this work.

decisions.decision: All monthly maths happens in Go over the fetched rows, in one place. One query returns the month's vehicle_metrics rows; the use case computes all-days, weekday and weekend figures from that slice.
decisions.why: The charging half must be Go anyway, since it arrives as []Entry and []Session through charging's ports. SQL would split one month's maths across two places. A month is ~30 rows.

decisions.decision: Only ONE new charging port is added (tier 1): the stored monthly_effective_capacity row for one exact (tesla_id, month). External charges use Reader.ListEntriesByVehicleBetween and supercharger sessions use SessionReader.ListSessionsByVehicleBetween, both of which already exist.
decisions.why: Verified in code. The ticket implied several new ports. Adding an existing read would widen charging's public surface for nothing, and the planned microservice split carries every port.

decisions.decision: The new Go type must not end in Processor, Manager, Handler, Helper, Data, Info, Object or Thing (make naming-guard fails new ones). It is written using the golang-naming, golang-code-style, golang-design-patterns, golang-data-structures and golang-documentation skills, additive to ai/go-conventions.md.
decisions.why: The ticket calls it a 'processor', which the guard rejects. The owner asked for the golang skills explicitly; they are not part of the pipeline's Doc-Pack by default.

tiers.notes: Read port for the stored monthly_effective_capacity of one exact (tesla_id, month). Must report 'no row' apart from 'row with NULL capacity'.
Migration creating ALL columns, sqlc queries, the use case type, the vehicle_metrics figures (RD2/RD6) and the copied capacity. Database design gate applies.
Fill ext_* split by ChargingType AC/DC, sc_*, and the three JSONB ending-battery distributions. Existing charging ports only (RD9).
Nightly step 5 after step 4. Runs EVERY night for the current and previous month (RD3). Failure logs and never fails the cycle.
